La [caché de `Workers`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/cache/) se sienta delante del `worker`, así que un acierto responde sin ejecutar nada. Por defecto no se cachea: una página solo entra si ella misma lo pide. Cuando entra dura una hora, y al publicar se purga por etiquetas.

Un único *middleware* para todas las respuestas: resuelve el idioma, carga las etiquetas de accesibilidad, decide la política de caché y estampa siete cabeceras de seguridad. El panel de edición queda fuera, porque trae las suyas.

26 rutas públicas, 24 componentes y 12 hojas de estilo, con [render bajo demanda](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/on-demand-rendering/) de `Astro`, que también es de Cloudflare [desde enero de 2026](https://blog.cloudflare.com/astro-joins-cloudflare/). Los idiomas no se separan por prefijo sino por *slug* traducido, así que la ruta alterna se resuelve contra el CMS y nunca se adivina: adivinarla devuelve un 404.

[`EmDash`](https://blog.cloudflare.com/emdash-wordpress/) no es un servicio contratado: es el CMS que Cloudflare publicó en abril de 2026 con licencia MIT como sucesor de WordPress, y que usa en [su propio blog](https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-blog-uses-emdash/) desde el 12 de agosto. Aquí inyecta 183 rutas bajo `/_emdash` en esta misma aplicación, con 7 colecciones y 43 entradas: mismo *script*, mismos enlaces de recursos, ninguna llamada de red. Los *plugins* de terceros son la excepción deliberada, y corren en un aislado aparte con [Worker Loader](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/worker-loader/), sin salida a internet.

El contenido en [`D1`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/), los ficheros en [`R2`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/) y las sesiones en [`KV`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/). Los estáticos no pasan por aquí: los sirve la capa de recursos sin llegar a despertar al `worker`.

Un fichero de texto en Git, más los cuerpos de los servicios en `markdown`. De ahí sale la web entera en una reconstrucción desde cero, que es lo que hace la integración continua antes de cada fusión.

The [`Workers` cache](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/cache/) sits in front of the `worker`, so a hit answers without running anything. Nothing is cached by default: a page only gets in if it asks to. Once in it lasts an hour, and publishing purges it by tag.

One *middleware* for every response: it resolves the locale, loads the accessibility labels, decides the cache policy and stamps seven security headers. The editing panel is excluded, because it brings its own.

26 public routes, 24 components and 12 stylesheets, on `Astro` [on-demand rendering](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/on-demand-rendering/) — Astro has been part of Cloudflare [since January 2026](https://blog.cloudflare.com/astro-joins-cloudflare/). Locales are not separated by prefix but by translated slug, so the alternate route is resolved against the CMS and never guessed: guessing it returns a 404.

[`EmDash`](https://blog.cloudflare.com/emdash-wordpress/) is not a service you subscribe to: it is the CMS Cloudflare released in April 2026 under an MIT licence as a successor to WordPress, and has run [its own blog](https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-blog-uses-emdash/) since 12 August. Here it injects 183 routes under `/_emdash` into this very application, with 7 collections and 43 entries: same *script*, same bindings, no network call. Third-party *plugins* are the deliberate exception, running in a separate isolate through [Worker Loader](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/worker-loader/), with no way out to the internet.

Content in [`D1`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/), files in [`R2`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/) and sessions in [`KV`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/). Static assets never come through here: the asset layer serves them without ever waking the `worker`.
A text file in Git, plus the service bodies in `markdown`. The whole site comes out of it in a rebuild from nothing, which is what continuous integration does before every merge.
The EmDash panel editing this very page, showing the title, the body and the publish state.
The panel, editing this page. It runs in the same worker that just served it to you.

El agente propone y no fusiona. Las comprobaciones rechazan y no escriben: su credencial es de solo lectura. La persona puede las dos cosas, y por eso es la única que puede equivocarse con nombre y apellidos. La letra pequeña: que el agente no fusione es una regla escrita, no un candado del servidor.
Antes de preguntarle nada a una persona, la rama pasa por dieciséis pasos que pueden fallar. Se niegan a dejar pasar lo que una revisión a ojo no ve:
un cliente que no puede salir en un repositorio público.
una etiqueta que solo existe en un idioma, o una frase escrita a fuego en la plantilla.
un literal o una anchura nueva, que es como vuelven las siete medidas distintas.
una llamada puesta donde las cabeceras ya se han ido, que no cachea nada y lo parece.
Imágenes que se piden a sí mismas:
una URL absoluta a nuestro propio dominio, que en Cloudflare no puede funcionar y en local no se nota.
tabulador, reflujo a 320 píxeles y validación del

Un guardia solo vale si puede fallar, y uno que no encuentra nada se ve igual que uno que no puede. Los más delicados llevan un control positivo que los revienta si dejan de mirar. La última puerta tampoco es automática: producción se despliega a mano.
Un número sin fecha es el peor sitio para la deriva, así que aquí hay dos clases y no se mezclan. El umbral vive en
: 95 o más en rendimiento, cien en accesibilidad, buenas prácticas y SEO, sobre la mediana de tres pasadas con emulación móvil.

La medición lleva su fecha. El 24 de agosto de 2026, sobre la construcción de producción: cien en las cuatro categorías y en las cinco direcciones, con el mayor contenido pintado por debajo de 1,6 segundos. Es la mediana de cada una, y la cota es la peor de las cinco.
El repositorio es público y se sincroniza con cada cambio en la rama principal, con la historia entera y sin filtrar. Publicar así tiene un coste: por eso existe el guardia de nombres no citables.
Código, semillas, comprobaciones y despliegues: está todo.

data.title: Deconstructing this website
data.excerpt: How this website is built, layer by layer: from the point of presence that answered your request to the commit that authorised these words. Thresholds and measurements in plain sight.

children.text: If someone tells you how they work and cannot show you the workshop, be suspicious. This is ours.
The tour runs downwards, from the point of presence that answered your request to the commit that authorised these words. Every layer opens if you want the detail, and everything claimed here is in
There are no servers to look after, and that is the least of it. What matters is where the response you are reading was made: at the
. Cache sits in front, and on a hit the code never runs.
, which Cloudflare released under an MIT licence as a successor to WordPress, and not a service to call over the network: it is the same application, served by the same
. And at the bottom of the descent there is no database, there is a text file in Git.
: the filename is the slug, the directory is the locale. A rebuild from nothing remakes the whole site, and
Caching inherits the discipline: a page is cached only if it asks to be, and publishing purges it by tag. One gap is worth saying out loud: menus and site settings emit no event, so a one-hour
A model writing the first draft is neither impressive nor mysterious. What decides whether this is serious is

The agent proposes and cannot merge. The checks refuse and cannot write: their credential is read-only. The human can do both, which is why the human is the only one who can be wrong by name. The small print: the agent not merging is a written rule, not a lock on the server.
Before a person is asked anything, the branch goes through sixteen steps that can fail. They refuse what a reading by eye does not catch:
a client who must not appear in a public repository.
a label that exists in one locale only, or a sentence burnt into a template.
a literal or a new width, which is how seven different measures come back.
a call placed after the headers have gone, which caches nothing and looks like it does.
an absolute URL to our own domain, which cannot work on Cloudflare and looks perfectly fine locally.
keyboard traversal, reflow at 320 pixels and

A guard is only worth having if it can fail, and one that finds nothing looks like one that cannot. The most delicate ones carry a positive control that blows them up the moment they stop looking. The last door is not automatic either: production is deployed by hand.
An undated number is the worst possible place for drift, so there are two kinds here and they never mix. The threshold lives in
: 95 or more for performance, 100 for accessibility, best practices and SEO, over the median of three runs under mobile emulation.

The measurement carries its date. On 24 August 2026, against the production build: 100 in all four categories across all five addresses, with the largest content painted in under 1.6 seconds. Each figure is a median, and the bound is the worst of the five.
The repository is public and syncs on every change to the main branch, whole history, unfiltered. Publishing like that has a cost: that is why the non-citable-names guard exists.
Code, seeds, checks and deployments: it is all there.
if you would do it differently.
